doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Two weeks with Sinatra, Ella and Basie, and Benny's good memory
summary: He calls the Sinatra run the week he'd relive, and tells a story showing Goodman remembered pianist Bill Miller's charts from 1935.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And people have asked me “if you wanted to re-live two weeks of your life, or a week in music, which week will you choose?” And I think it would be those two weeks with him. I used to sit on the stage, Monk — they’d do “The Lady is a Tramp” to finish, you know,

he and Ella with the Basie band. You’re Ella, I mean you’re Basie, and facing the other way, and I’m this close to you. And there’s reams of music, reams of music, and Basie’s looking going clink, you know. Frank goes “I get too hungry” and Basie goes bonk bonk, bonk bonk. All this music. So finally one night Frank sang “I get too hungry/for dinner at eight.” And Basie goes [scats] and Sinatra turns around and said, “Bill, be careful, you might get a hernia.” But oh, he was so great. And out of all the people I’ve ever, ever spoken to, and I’ve played and met the Queen Mother twice, no one gave me the sensation that I experienced with Frank Sinatra. He had the most beautiful face, to look at him. Beautiful teeth. And you think you’ve seen blue eyes? You’ve never seen blue eyes like those. But the speaking voice. It was like he was singing to me you know. He would come up occasionally and say, “How is everything going,” you know. And then one night Benny came, and this is one to prove to you Benny had a good memory. We had dinner beforehand, Benny and I, and he came to the theater to hear Frank you see? And he also wrote a letter to the government on my behalf to get me permission to work with him for two weeks with Benny Goodman, see? I wish I had got a copy of that letter, it was really something. Anyway, Benny said to me, “Who’s playing the piano for Frank?” I said, “It’s Bill Miller.” “Bill Miller, oh, yes,” he said, “yes, yes, Bill. He did a couple of charts for the band.” I said, “Oh, did he?” He said, “Say hello tonight, for me.” I said, “Okay.” So I get to work and I said, “Bill, I just had dinner with Benny and he told me that you wrote a couple of charts for the band.” So Bill said, “No, I never wrote for the band, uh, my God” he said, “1935 when I was in high school, I remember now.” Benny remembered all that way back.
